evidence: Abstract: "adenosine signaling is associated with reduced efficacy of anti-PD1 therapy in published cohorts"
note: Explicit.

evidence: Abstract: "the APM score was significantly higher in responders compared with non-responders"; "a higher APM score was associated with improved OS"
note: Explicit.

evidence: Full text (PMC6879305): "Breast cancer and prostate cancer have usual TMB but fairly low ICI-response rates, probably because of low APS." APS-ORR correlation 0.42 (p=0.038)
note: Abstract gives no direction; full text does (positive APS-ORR correlation across cancer types). Main predictor in paper is TIGS (TMB x APS); gene list = APS genes.

evidence: Title: "A gene expression signature associated with B cells predicts benefit from immune checkpoint blockade in lung adenocarcinoma"; abstract: "B cells (AUC = 0.77, p = .0055) ... predicted benefit of ICB"
note: Explicit.

evidence: Abstract: "B cell markers were the most differentially expressed genes in the tumours of responders versus non-responders"
note: Full text (PMC8762581): B-cell genes and MCP-counter B-cell signature higher in responders at baseline.

evidence: Full text (PMC5557000): "all eight evaluable predictive genes were in fact down-regulated in the non-responders relative to responders."
note: Whole-blood (not tumour) classifier for tremelimumab (anti-CTLA-4): "9 predictors and six non-predictive enhancer variables"; an unweighted score of all 15 genes is an approximation of the published model.

evidence: Abstract: "this signature is a predictor of the failure of PD-1 blockade"; full text (PMC6224529): "the C-ECM-up score was significantly higher in progressors"
note: IMPLEMENTATION CAVEAT: the paper scores C-ECM-up (30 genes) and C-ECM-down (28 genes) separately and the resistance direction is for C-ECM-up. The SignatureSets file merges both (rows 1-28 TNXB..MFAP5 = down set by gene identity; rows 29-58 MMP11..ADAM12 = up set) into one 58-gene ssGSEA set.

evidence: Abstract: "CCL5 and CXCL9 coexpression revealed immunoreactive tumors with prolonged survival and response to checkpoint blockade."
note: Explicit.

evidence: Abstract: "Higher baseline frequency of CD39+ CD8+ T cells conferred improved clinical outcomes from ICB therapy." ... "a gene signature of CD39+ CD8+ T cells predicted benefit from ICB, but not chemotherapy"
note: DISAGREES: label "resistance" is the opposite of the paper (signature predicted benefit from anti-PD-L1 in a phase III NSCLC trial). The SignatureSets information text itself also says it was a predictor of response.

evidence: Full text (PMC6641984): "CD8_G cells were enriched in responding lesions" ... CD8_G markers "(e.g. IL7R, TCF7, REL, FOXP1, FOSL2 and STAT4)"
note: Abstract does not say which state goes with response; full text does. Gene list (IL7R, TCF7, REL, FOXP1, FOSL2, STAT4 ...) is the responder-associated CD8_G state.

evidence: Abstract: "Net overexpression of this signature was predictive of poor clinical outcome in 12 cancer data sets"
note: Prognostic chromosomal-instability signature (2006); no immunotherapy data. "resistance" is an extrapolation (e.g. from aneuploidy literature), not a finding of this paper.

evidence: Abstract: "Net overexpression of this signature was predictive of poor clinical outcome in 12 cancer data sets"
note: As CIN25: prognostic only; no ICB direction in source.

evidence: Abstract: "...that predicts resistance uniquely to blockade of CTLA-4, but not PD-1."
note: Explicit; note the paper restricts the resistance effect to anti-CTLA-4 (not anti-PD-1).

evidence: Full text (PMC6487502): "a higher CTL level indicates a better patient survival, but only when TGFB1 has a low expression level."
note: CTL level (mean of CD8A, CD8B, GZMA, GZMB, PRF1) is an infiltration estimate used inside TIDE; the paper does not test CTL alone against ICB response. Survival benefit is conditional on absence of dysfunction. "sensitive" is plausible but not reported.

evidence: Abstract: "highly aneuploid tumors show reduced expression of markers of cytotoxic infiltrating immune cells, especially CD8+ T cells"; title: "...correlates with markers of immune evasion and with reduced response to immunotherapy"
note: DISAGREES (by direct inference): the cytotoxic-marker score was not itself tested against ICB outcome, but the paper places low cytotoxic infiltrate in the aneuploid tumours with poorer ICB survival; a separate 23-gene aneuploidy-up/immune-down signature was linked to worse survival on immunotherapy (full text PMC5592794). No reading supports high cytotoxic score = resistance; label appears to transfer the aneuploidy direction to the immune score.

evidence: Abstract: "was also associated with better overall survival of the subset of melanoma patients"
note: Title proposes "potential for patient selection for immunotherapy?" but no ICB-treated cohort; higher score = lymph-node-like structures and better OS (prognostic). Direction would be sensitivity if anything; consistent with label but not an ICB finding.

evidence: Abstract: "patients whose tumors responded to ICB had higher scores in an inflammatory gene signature" ... "or a more epithelial phenotype"; "reversal of EMT might augment efficacy of ICB"
note: Gene weights (epithelial -1, mesenchymal +1) make a higher score = more mesenchymal = non-response.

evidence: Abstract: "higher EMT/stroma-related gene expression is associated with lower response rates"
note: Explicit (nivolumab, urothelial cancer).

evidence: Abstract: "We also found that both continuous TMB and immune GEP (or tumor infiltrating lymphocytes) independently predicted pCR."
note: GEP is "a previously developed immune GEP for pathological complete remission (pCR)" (GeparSixto, chemotherapy). Endpoint is pCR in chemotherapy +/- durvalumab (GeparNuevo); abstract does not show the association is ICB-specific. Full text not open access.

evidence: Full text (PMC5531419): the refined IFN-gamma and expanded immune signatures "both showed statistically significant associations with improved clinical outcome"
note: Abstract covers only the GEP; full text gives direction for the 6-gene IFN-gamma signature.

evidence: Full text (PMC6693632): "High scores predict good response."
note: SignatureSets implements IMPRES as a weighted mean of +/-1 genes, not the published 15 pairwise gene-gene comparisons; direction of weights is consistent with the published pairs.

evidence: Full text (PMC7862369): "elevated expression levels of IMS genes were observed in patients from the nonresponder groups in the IFN-γ+ subgroup"
note: DISAGREES: IMS = immunosuppression signature (FAP, PDGFRB, CD163, IL10, CCL2, AXL, VCAN ...); higher in non-responders; the predictor of response is the IFN-gamma/IMS RATIO, not IMS. SignatureSets info text itself says IMS genes are "associated with negative response to ICB". Journal: npj Genomic Medicine.

evidence: Full text (PMC5531419): the refined IFN-gamma and expanded immune signatures "both showed statistically significant associations with improved clinical outcome"
note: Gene list = expanded immune signature minus LAG3 (17 of 18 genes).

evidence: Abstract: "the 11-IRG signature low-risk group, which possessed a higher IPS, represented a more immunogenic phenotype"; full text (PMC6844304): "High-risk patients had poorer OS than low-risk patients."
note: Paper: higher Cox risk score = poorer OS and (in silico, TCGA immunophenoscore; no ICB-treated cohort) less likely ICI response -> opposite of "sensitive". BUT the SignatureSets +/-1 weights equal the Table 2 tumour-vs-normal "Regulation" column, not the Cox coefficient signs (LEPR, PRL, NRP1, ANGPTL5 have positive coefficients but weight -1; IFI30 negative coefficient but +1), so the implemented score is not the paper's risk score and its ICB direction is undetermined.

evidence: Full text (PMC7545100): patients "may respond to the less toxic anti-PD-1 treatment alone if the z-score is >0.19"; abstract: γδ T cells "overrepresented in the non-responding tumors"
note: Paper uses a nearest-centroid classifier; its z-score (higher = response) is not an unsigned gene-set score. The 109 genes mix markers of non-responder-enriched TREM2hi macrophages/γδ T cells (e.g. TREM2, SPP1, MMP9, CCL18) and a responder-enriched B-cell subset; direction of an unsigned GSVA score is not determined by the paper (title: signature "of TREM2hi macrophages and γδ T cells").

evidence: Full text (PMC5819607): "a significant positive correlation was observed between TCR clonality and immune scores in pre-PD-1 blockade samples"; abstract: "a more clonal T cell repertoire was predictive of response to PD-1"
note: Indirect: no responder vs non-responder comparison of the immune score itself was found in the text; score correlates positively with a response marker (clonality) and negatively with copy-number-loss burden (higher in non-responders).

evidence: Abstract: "Multivariate analysis revealed that immune score is a strong predictor of patient survival and the response to immunotherapy"; "High immune score is significantly associated with BRCA1/2 mutation status and the response to chemotherapy."
note: Ovarian cancer, public non-ICB data (chemotherapy); no ICB-treated cohort identified and no ICB direction given. Higher score = better survival and chemosensitivity, so consistent with "sensitive" if anything. Full text not in PMC.

evidence: Abstract: "patients whose tumors responded to ICB had higher scores in an inflammatory gene signature"
note: Explicit.

evidence: Abstract: "a high KDM5A gene signature correlated with KDM5A expression and could potentially serve as a marker of response"
note: Mainly mouse models; direction explicit.

evidence: Abstract: "Progression-free survival (PFS) was significantly longer in patients with high M1 signature ... high peripheral T cell signature scores"
note: NSCLC (SignatureSets cancer.type says melanoma). Explicit.

evidence: Full text (PMC6898788): "expression of all 13 MHC-II-associated HLA genes was higher in responders"; "low MHC-II expression was associated with primary resistance"
note: Abstract gives no direction; full text explicit.

evidence: Full text (PMC6898788): "MHC-I antigen-presentation genes all trended toward having higher expression in responders" ... "but none passed the statistical significance threshold"
note: Direction is a non-significant trend only.

evidence: Full text (PMC8482620): "Nonresponder melanomas consistently exhibited significantly higher MPS scores than responders"
note: Abstract gives no direction; full text explicit. SignatureSets signs (33 +1 / 12 -1) match "33 upregulated and 12 downregulated genes in M1/M2" (counts checked, not gene by gene).

evidence: Full text (PMC5319024): "Under anti-PD1 therapy, most cell types were more than 4.2 units higher"; abstract: "they separate responders and non-responders early on therapy"
note: Descriptive cell-type marker paper; macrophage score not singled out for an ICB direction; illustration is on-treatment. Also: "Enrichment of DCs, neutrophils and macrophages generally indicates poor prognosis" (TCGA). Weakly consistent with "sensitive".

evidence: Full text (PMC8762581): myeloid DCs appear only as an MCP-counter population ("myeloid dendritic cells and neutrophils"); no responder/non-responder direction stated in text or legends.
note: Gene list = MCP-counter myeloid DC genes (CD1A, CD1B, CD1E, CLEC10A, CLIC2, WFDC21P). SignatureSets claims "significantly more expressed in non-responder"; could be in a figure panel but not verifiable from the text.

evidence: Full text (PMC7519254): "we found 85 genes that were up-regulated in responders and 69 genes that were up-regulated in nonresponders"; "patients scoring highly for the nonresponder signature with worse survival"
note: Direction by construction (mouse CD8 TILs). Human ICB bulk cohorts: "we did not observe significant associations of our derived gene signatures with response". SignatureSets list has 258 genes vs 69 in text; provenance not verified.

evidence: Full text (PMC5650537, review): "a higher response rate and longer PFS and overall survival were observed in patients with PD-L1-positive tumours"
note: Review of PD-L1 IHC (protein), not a gene signature; it also notes "contradictory results regarding the role of PD-L1 expression as a marker of response". Second PMID (TIDE) uses PD-L1 only as a comparator.

evidence: Full text (PMC7140048): "of which 152 were downregulated and 127 were upregulated in MITFlow/PTENneg tumors"; "patients with MITFlow/PTENneg classified melanomas were associated with inferior patient survival"
note: Paper: centroid classifier; MITFlow/PTENneg class = worse survival incl. ICB cohorts. BUT SignatureSets file = 263 genes all weight +1 (weighted mean). By gene identity rows 1-150 (ITGB7..MLANA: CD8A, CXCL9, CXCL10, GZMB, HLA-B, STAT1, MITF, TYR, MLANA) are the immune/melanocytic block DOWN in the poor-outcome class and rows 151-263 (CADM1..SPRY1: adhesion/ECM/Wnt) are UP. An unsigned mean mixes opposite directions and, dominated by the immune block, may track benefit, opposite to the label.

evidence: Full text (PMC7519254): "we found 85 genes that were up-regulated in responders and 69 genes that were up-regulated in nonresponders"
note: Direction by construction (mouse CD8 TILs). No significant association in human ICB bulk cohorts. SignatureSets list has 443 genes vs 85 in text; provenance not verified.

evidence: Zemek 2019 abstract: "responsive tumors were characterized by an inflammatory gene expression signature" ... "up-regulation of signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1)"
note: Gene module from Care 2015 (DLBCL; "This response is associated with improved outcome", not ICB). ICB direction from Zemek 2019 (mouse models).

evidence: Abstract: "Lack of response was associated with a signature of transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) signalling in fibroblasts."
note: Explicit.

evidence: Abstract: "TIS scores were significantly associated with complete or partial response to anti-PD-1 treatment in the whole cohort"
note: Explicit.

evidence: Title: "Tertiary lymphoid structures improve immunotherapy and survival in melanoma"; abstract: "We derived a gene signature associated with tertiary lymphoid structures, which predicted clinical outcomes in cohorts of patients treated with immune checkpoint blockade"
note: Direction from title plus abstract (signature marks TLS, which improve outcome); score direction not stated in the abstract; full text paywalled.

evidence: Abstract: "Therapeutic strategies based on antiangiogenic approaches are beginning to show great promise in clinical studies."
note: Ovarian tumour endothelium vs normal endothelium; no immunotherapy or outcome association in the source. "resistance" is not derived from this paper.

evidence: Abstract: "We identified a resistance program expressed by malignant cells that is associated with T cell exclusion"
note: Gene list (ribosomal, MYC targets, MAGEA4/MAGEC1) is the up-regulated arm of the program (by gene identity).

evidence: Full text (PMC5531419): "All genes in the signature, except CD276, are positively associated with improved clinical outcome."
note: Explicit.

evidence: Abstract: "pre-existing immunity, defined by high T-effector-interferon-γ-associated gene expression, had improved overall survival with atezolizumab"
note: Explicit (POPLAR).

evidence: Full text (PMC6721896): "High Teff gene signature expression, based on median signature score, was associated with improved ORR" ... within the atezolizumab + bevacizumab arm
note: SignatureSets info says "anti-PD-L1 and sunitinib"; actually atezolizumab + bevacizumab (sunitinib was the comparator).

evidence: Abstract: "The predictive power of VIGex-Hot was observed in a cohort of 98 refractory solid tumor" patients treated with immunotherapy
note: Hot = highest VIGex scores; direction implied by abstract (Med 2023); full text not in PMC.

evidence: Abstract: "activation of the WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway contributed to the development of a noninflamed TME" ... "which results in resistance to PD-1 blockade therapy"
note: Explicit.

evidence: Abstract: "Progression-free survival (PFS) was significantly longer in patients with high M1 signature ... high peripheral T cell signature scores"
note: Explicit (NSCLC, anti-PD-1).

evidence: Full text (PMC6359802): "a highly or poorly proliferative tumor microenvironment is associated with limited sensitivity to ICIs"; "There was a significant survival advantage for moderately proliferative tumors"
note: Non-monotonic (moderate best, both extremes worse): no single direction for a higher score. "resistance" matches only the high-vs-moderate contrast.
